title: Basic labelled-tail deletion identities
statement: For every linearly ordered type I, p and t, there exists an equivalence e between cechTailOutgoingIndex p t and cechTailIncomingIndex p t such that for every x there is k satisfying k.val + 1 = x.val.2.2.2.val, x.val.2.2.1 k = (e x).val.1, the restriction identity for all z, and x.val.2.1.val = (e x).val.2.2.1.val.

source.place: Tag 01FM, cohomology-equation-first-homotopy (20.23.6.1), omitted verification; unsigned tail-deletion part; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01FM

proof.text: For an outgoing quadruple, set k=r-1, j=tau(k), and d=sigma^{-1}(j). The nonjunction and tail conditions imply a<=k and a<d. Restrict sigma and tau via the increasing omission maps to obtain permutations rho and eta, and retain the prefix length b=a. Restriction preserves stable sorting and partial sorting. The stable ordering of the pairs (t(label),label) implies the incoming inequality. These constructions give a function with the required four identities.

The function is injective: stable-sort uniqueness identifies sigma, the retained prefix identity identifies a, partial-sort uniqueness identifies tau, and the omitted label determines k=tau^{-1}(j), hence r=k+1.

For surjectivity, start with (j,rho,b,eta). Let sigma=Tuple.sort(t) and d=sigma^{-1}(j). Stable-sort uniqueness identifies rho with the restriction of sigma deleting d. The incoming inequality implies b<d. Take a=b.castSucc and the unique partial sort tau for sigma with prefix a. Set k=tau^{-1}(j) and r=k+1. Prefix agreement implies a<=k. Deleting k from tau is a partial sort of rho with prefix b, hence equals eta by uniqueness. The resulting outgoing quadruple maps to the given incoming quadruple. Apply Equiv.ofBijective and the explicit deletion identities.

lean.statement:
theorem cechTailDeletionBasic {I : Type v} [LinearOrder I] (p : ℕ)
    (t : Fin (p + 2) → I) :
    ∃ e : cechTailOutgoingIndex p t ≃ cechTailIncomingIndex p t,
      ∀ x, ∃ k : Fin (p + 2),
        k.val + 1 = x.val.2.2.2.val ∧
        x.val.2.2.1 k = (e x).val.1 ∧
        (∀ z, x.val.2.2.1 (k.succAbove z) =
          (e x).val.1.succAbove ((e x).val.2.2.2 z)) ∧
        x.val.2.1.val = (e x).val.2.2.1.val
